info.title: twotrack API
info.description:
Supply-chain agent console API. LLMs route and narrate; code computes.

Every endpoint except `/api/health`, `/api/auth/login` and `/api/auth/demo` needs
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`; `POST /api/auth/logout` revokes the token it is called with.
Errors share one shape: `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`.

Language. Labels and messages come in English and Chinese. `POST /api/query` follows the
language of the question. Every other endpoint that words something follows `Accept-Language`:
when it asks for `zh` (or `zh-CN` ...) first the text is Chinese; anything else, and no header
at all, gives English. Endpoints that return rows return ids and values, never labels; the
labels of entities and fields come from `GET /api/entities`.

get.description:
Liveness for load balancers and the console's banner. Needs no sign-in and reveals
nothing beyond the version, whether the instance is a demo, which language model answers
(its name and model id; never an endpoint or a key) and the import limits.

post.description:
Passwordless sign-in as the built-in demo user of a role. Exists only when the server
runs with ``TWOTRACK_DEMO_MODE=1``; otherwise the route answers 404 as if it were absent.

Sign out: revoke the token this request was made with.

The token is refused from now on with `401 token_revoked`, on this server and after a
restart (its id goes on a deny-list kept until the token would have expired anyway). Other
tokens of the same user, on other devices, keep working. Signing out twice with the same
token answers 401 the second time: the token is already dead.

Route a question to a registered tool or workflow and answer it.

The language model only routes and narrates; every number comes from code, and the rows
in the answer are never shown to a model.

The language of the answer and of every label in it (the tool's `label` in `provenance`,
in `clarify_options` and in `approval`) is detected from the text of the question, not
from `Accept-Language`: a Chinese question gets a Chinese answer.

200.description: `text/event-stream` by default: `trace` frames (TraceStep), then one `response` frame (QueryOut) or one `error` frame (ErrorEnvelope); `: heartbeat` comment lines every 15 s while the server works. With `?stream=false`: a QueryOut.

get.description:
Confirmations waiting to be approved: the caller's own; an admin sees everyone's.

`label` and `summary` are worded in the language `Accept-Language` asks for (`zh`, `zh-CN`
...: Chinese; anything else, or no header: English), whatever language the question was
asked in. `expires_in_s` is the time left on the server's clock: count down from it as of
receipt instead of comparing `expires_at` with the browser's clock.

post.description:
Run the request this confirmation guards, once. Only its requester may approve.

The outcome of an import is worded in the language `Accept-Language` asks for (`zh`,
`zh-CN` ...: Chinese; anything else, or no header: English). A confirmed question runs and
is narrated in the language the question was asked in, like the answer it continues.

Refusals: 403 `not_requester`; 409 `not_submitted` (an upload not yet committed for
approval) or `grant_used` (it already ran, or another approval has taken it and is running
it: approving again never runs it twice, however close the two approvals are); 410
`approval_expired`; an import's own (such as 409 `digest_mismatch`); 404 for an id that
was never issued or a confirmation that was rejected. Each 403, 409 and 410 leaves an audit
record under the grant id (`GET /api/audit?grant_id=`) with the reason in `problem`; a
rejected confirmation already has the record that says why.

get.description:
Root entities with their category children, fields limited to what the role may see.

Every `label` and `description` (entity, category, field) is in the language
`Accept-Language` asks for (`zh`, `zh-CN` ...: Chinese; anything else, or no header:
English). A text a plugin did not translate is its English one.

A page of records. Every other query parameter is an equality filter on a field id
(`?status=active`); repeat it for several values (`?status=a&status=b` matches either).
`sort`, `page` and `page_size` are reserved names.

post.description:
Validate an upload against the entity. Nothing is written.

Everything the response says in words is in the language `Accept-Language` asks for (`zh`,
`zh-CN` ...: Chinese; anything else, or no header: English): the label of each mapped
column, the problems of each row, the confirmation's label and summary, and the message
of a file that is refused (an empty file, one named `.xlsx` that is no workbook, missing or
colliding columns ...).

400.description: The request is malformed or names something that does not exist

403.description: The caller's role may not do this

post.description:
Write the valid rows of a previewed upload.

Without `grant_id` this asks for confirmation (`needs_confirmation`, and the approval
appears in `/api/approvals`). With the `grant_id` from the preview or that approval it
writes now. Either way only the user who previewed can commit.

The approval's `label` and `summary`, and the message of a refusal, are worded in the
language `Accept-Language` asks for (`zh`, `zh-CN` ...: Chinese; anything else, or no
header: English).

ApprovalItem.title: ApprovalItem
ApprovalItem.description:
A confirmation waiting in the list. ``label``, ``summary`` and ``expires_in_s`` are
worded for this request (``Accept-Language``); see ``ApprovalRef``.

model_errors.title: Model Errors
model_errors.description: Model calls that failed while answering, in order (the call, the error class, the HTTP status). The answer fell back without them: routing to rules and BM25, narration to the template (answer_source `template`). Empty when every call succeeded or no model call was made.

ApprovalOutcome.title: ApprovalOutcome
ApprovalOutcome.description:
What running an approved request produced. ``status`` is the pipeline's verdict:
only ``ok`` means the write happened.

ApprovalRef.title: ApprovalRef
ApprovalRef.description:
A pending one-time confirmation. ``grant_id`` is public; the token never leaves the
server. Approve it with ``POST /api/approvals/{grant_id}/approve`` before ``expires_at``.

``expires_in_s`` is the time left when the response was made, on the server's clock and
never below 0: count down from it as of receipt rather than comparing ``expires_at`` with
the browser's clock, which may be off. ``label`` names what is confirmed (the tool's
title, or the import) in the reply language.

``target`` is the id of what is confirmed, the one the audit log records: the tool or
workflow the grant is bound to (``create_po``), or ``import:<entity>`` for an import. A
write the exploration agent proposed has no routed target (``decision.target`` is null), so
this is where its id is. Null only when the request is no longer stored and nothing else
names it.

AuditStatsOut.title: AuditStatsOut
AuditStatsOut.description:
Records per route source and outcome in a window: pipeline runs, plus the queries that
were answered without one (``clarify``, ``chat``), so the shares cover every routing
decision. ``started`` intent records are left out, so each pipeline run counts once. A
query that no arm could place (the chat fallback) counts under ``fallback``, not under
``semantic`` (a BM25 pick). Records written without a route source (an approval-side
refusal) count under ``none``, the value ``GET /api/audit?route_source=none`` lists them
by.

file.title: File
file.description: CSV or XLSX; the type is detected from the content

ClarifyOption.title: ClarifyOption
ClarifyOption.description:
A target the user may pick. The client re-sends the question with ``explicit_target=
name`` and, when set, ``explicit_params`` exactly as given here.

FieldError.title: FieldError
FieldError.description: One problem of one preview row, for the cell it is about.

LogoutOut.title: LogoutOut
LogoutOut.description: The caller's token is revoked: it is refused from now on (``token_revoked``).

ModelCallError.title: ModelCallError
ModelCallError.description:
A model call that failed, as the trace and the answer record it. Never the error's
message, the request or the key: a message may echo the request.

ProviderInfo.title: ProviderInfo
ProviderInfo.description: Which language model answers. Never an endpoint URL or a key.

model_errors.title: Model Errors
model_errors.description: Model calls that failed while answering, in order (the call, the error class, the HTTP status). The answer fell back without them: routing to rules and BM25, narration to the template (answer_source `template`). Empty when every call succeeded or no model call was made.

QueryOut.title: QueryOut
QueryOut.description:
The engine's answer. ``rows`` are the table the signed-in user may see (projected for
their role); the language model never receives them.

Role.title: Role
Role.description: Fixed v0.1 role set. ``admin`` passes every role allow-list.

ScopeCheck.title: ScopeCheck
ScopeCheck.description: What routing found about the constraints a question names, for one routed target.

ScopeChoice.title: ScopeChoice
ScopeChoice.description: One way to continue after a scope clarification: run ``target`` explicitly.

ScopeMention.title: ScopeMention
ScopeMention.description: A constraint the question names, e.g. category *packaging* or warehouse *WH-EAST*.

UploadLimits.title: UploadLimits
UploadLimits.description:
What an import accepts (the upload guard's settings): a larger file or more data rows
is refused before any row is read.
